lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Guided practice B: interpreting conditional probability in context

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read once, then cover the example and try the guided set from memory.

items.prompt: 30 people; 18 do A, 14 do B, 7 do both. Find P(A or B).

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: An event has probability 1/8 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 13 successes and 6 failures; group Y with 13 successes and 10 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 5/10, P(B) = 4/10, and P(A and B) = 20/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).

items.prompt: In a group of 35, 20 do activity A, 12 do activity B, and 4 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: An event has probability 3/4 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 14 successes and 14 failures; group Y with 7 successes and 29 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 1/10, P(B) = 4/10, and P(A and B) = 5/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).

items.prompt: In a group of 69, 37 do activity A, 25 do activity B, and 16 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
